body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. We’re starting the week with a warm one — expect a high near 98° today under sunny skies. Overnight, a grass fire flared up on the northwest side, and deputies handled disturbances across the county. **KGET 17 reports that** the Kern County Homeless Collaborative has named a new director, and **23ABC tells us** that local leaders are pushing for stronger fireworks regulations after the Fourth of July. Let’s get to the news.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most notable call was a grass fire that broke out just after 2:20 a.m. near Nord Avenue and Hageman Road. Dispatchers received reports of flames in a field known for bonfires, with witnesses saying they saw people leaving the area. Fire crews from Engine 67, Engine 65, Truck 65, and Battalion 6 responded, finding about a half-acre of brush and grass burning. An additional engine was called in, and an Edwards Air Force Base water tender was offered as backup. The fire was contained to the field, with no structures threatened.

Elsewhere in Kern County, deputies and officers handled a string of disturbances. Around 10:54 p.m., a vehicle fled into a dirt field near Morning Drive, prompting Air 1 to circle overhead. Multiple off-road vehicles were reported in the area, and a citywide attempt-to-locate alert went out. Around 11:28 p.m., a caller reported a large gathering of 150 to 250 vehicles in a furniture store parking lot, drawing multiple units and another request for Air 1. No further updates were heard on the air before the feed moved on.

Fire crews also checked out a couple of smaller incidents that didn’t grow into anything serious. Around 9:25 p.m., Engine 46 was dispatched to an outside fire in a rural county area, though the exact location was garbled on the air. Later, around 1:04 a.m., crews responded to a report of AC smoke on East 19th Street, which turned out to be nothing significant. Deputies also fielded calls about disturbances, including a verbal altercation on Goodman Street and a report of subjects attempting to attack a caller in a white van west of the AM/PM on Highway 119.

## Today's weather

Today’s forecast calls for a high near 98° and a low around 72° tonight. It’s currently 70° at Meadows Field (KBFL) under clear skies. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and air quality is holding steady at a good level with an AQI of 48. Expect plenty of sunshine throughout the day, with conditions staying dry and warm as we head into the week.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that** the Kern County Homeless Collaborative has named a new director to lead its efforts in addressing homelessness. The collaborative, which brings together local agencies and nonprofits, plays a key role in coordinating services and housing for those in need. The new director will oversee initiatives aimed at reducing homelessness and connecting individuals with resources, a move that comes as the county continues to grapple with the challenges of housing insecurity.

**23ABC tells us** that Bakersfield’s police and fire chiefs presented their Fourth of July reports during a recent meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents. Despite a 6% drop in fire-related responses compared to last year, officials emphasized that stronger measures are needed to deter the use of illegal fireworks. City Councilman Eric Arias said policymakers are exploring code changes to address the issue, underscoring the need for community-wide efforts to ensure safety during future holidays.

**According to 23ABC**, Kern County supervisors are exploring a proposal that would place Kern and dozens of other counties in a new state, separate from coastal California. The effort, led by District 3 Supervisor Jeff Flores, aims to draw attention to the region’s industries and way of life. An economic analysis presented to the board found that the proposed inland state would account for only about 15% of California’s current real GDP, raising questions about the potential economic impact of such a move. CSU Bakersfield economics professor Richard Gearhart cautioned that separation could result in significant economic losses and reduced opportunities for growth.

## Something good

In a bit of uplifting news, **KGET 17 reports that** the Bakersfield and Tehachapi airports will receive a portion of the $109 million in federal aviation funding. This investment will support improvements and upgrades at both airports, ensuring they remain safe and efficient for travelers. The funding is part of a broader effort to enhance aviation infrastructure across the country, and it’s a welcome boost for our local facilities.

## Coming up this week

As we look ahead to the rest of the week, several public meetings and events are on the calendar. The Multi Modal Transportation And Traffic Safety Committee will meet on Wednesday, August 18, at 12:00 p.m. The Planning Commission is set to convene on Friday, August 20, at 5:30 p.m. Also on Wednesday, the Historic Preservation Commission will gather at 4:00 p.m., and the Water Board will meet on Thursday, August 19, at 10:00 a.m. The Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission is scheduled to meet on Tuesday, August 18, at 2:00 p.m.

For those looking for entertainment, the Fox Theater has a lineup of shows coming up. On Sunday, August 22, Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, and Grupo Yndio will take the stage. Comedian Rodney Carrington will perform on Thursday, August 27. CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE is set for Friday, August 28, followed by Willie Barcena on Saturday, August 29. Also on Saturday, Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix will be held. Rounding out the month, the MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA will take place on Friday, September 4.

That’s your brief for this Monday morning. Have a great week, and we’ll see you back here tomorrow.
